# mnemo-jvm-warden

> JVM-aware in-place vertical memory right-sizing for Kubernetes (1.35+): shrinks and grows running JVM pods without restarts or OOMKills, and lets Java applications request temporary memory leases through a local sidecar API.

Warden coordinates an ordered handshake between the JVM (`SoftMaxHeapSize` on ZGC/Shenandoah, forced GC and uncommit on G1) and Kubernetes In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling, so a pod is only shrunk after the JVM has verifiably released the memory. Standard VPA is JVM-blind: it can resize the pod but cannot make the JVM give memory back.

- **Safety handshake.** Shrink: lower JVM soft heap / cache, force a deep GC, verify actual RSS is under the target limit, then resize the pod down. Grow: resize the pod up, wait for cgroup headroom, then raise the JVM soft heap.
- **Components.** `warden-controller` (cluster-wide, reconciles `WardenPolicy` and `WardenBoost`), `warden-agent` (native sidecar per pod, needs `shareProcessNamespace: true`, JMX and a read-only host cgroup mount).
- **Supported collectors.** ZGC and Shenandoah (settable soft heap ceiling). G1 works with a weaker guarantee: no live soft-max, so the workload must launch with `-Xmx` already covering its largest target. Serial is not supported.
- **Requirements.** Kubernetes 1.35+ (In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling GA) and a Cluster Autoscaler or equivalent to turn lower requests into savings.
- **Install.** Helm repo `https://baokhang83.github.io/mnemo-jvm-warden/` (charts `warden` and `warden-sidecar`).
- **Java lease client.** Maven Central `io.github.baokhang83.mnemo:warden-boost-client:0.2.1` (Java 21, no third-party dependencies).

## Core documentation

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/README.md): Overview, Warden vs. VPA table, shrink/grow sequence diagram, Helm quick start, requirements and status.
- [Why Warden](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/docs/why-warden.md): The gap Warden fills, where the savings come from, and the JVM knobs Warden drives.
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/docs/architecture.md): Controller and sidecar topology, the resize state machine, failure modes and invariants.
- [Configuration reference and runbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/docs/configuration.md): `WardenPolicy` spec, agent and controller settings, Helm chart values, operator runbook.

## Custom resource definitions and samples

- [WardenPolicy CRD](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/charts/warden/crds/wardenpolicy-crd.yaml): Schedules and memory profiles.
- [WardenBoost CRD](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/charts/warden/crds/wardenboost-crd.yaml): On-demand, application-driven memory claims (experimental).
- [Sample WardenPolicy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/deploy/wardenpolicy-sample-valid.yaml): A valid policy to start from.
- [Sample Pod with sidecar and Boost RBAC](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/deploy/example-sidecar-boost.yaml): ServiceAccount, Role and a Pod running the Warden sidecar with the Boost API.

## Boost API and security

- [Warden Boost operator guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/docs/warden-boost.md): Experimental memory leases, loopback sidecar API, Java lease client, ValidatingAdmissionPolicy setup.
- [Boost compatibility and operations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/docs/warden-boost-operations.md): Tested compatibility, first-response steps, release verification.
- [Threat model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/docs/threat-model.md): Assets, actors, trust boundaries, abuse cases for `shareProcessNamespace`, host cgroup, JMX and tokens.
- [Operator hardening guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/docs/hardening.md): What must hold for the trust model to be true.
- [RBAC-to-code-path mapping](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/docs/rbac-mapping.md): Which permission each code path needs.

## Guides and external articles

- [How to shrink JVM memory in Kubernetes without a restart](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/baokhang83/mnemo-jvm-warden/main/docs/shrink-jvm-memory-kubernetes.md): Why JVM pods get OOMKilled after in-place resize, how to size the smallest memory limit, and why VPA alone is not enough.
- [Walkthrough: Your JVMs Are Burning Money Overnight](https://baokhang.hashnode.dev/shrink-jvm-memory-kubernetes-in-place-resize): Hands-on tutorial with a three-replica Spring Boot deployment on kind.
- [warden-boost-client on Maven Central](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/io.github.baokhang83.mnemo/warden-boost-client): Published Java lease client.
